newsitem.title: YEMEN: London court to meet on Yemen-Eritrea row.
newsitem.headline: London court to meet on Yemen-Eritrea row.

text.p: An arbitration court agreed by Yemen and Eritrea will hold its first meeting this month on how to resolve their dispute over Red Sea islands on busy oil tanker routes, a Yemeni Foreign Ministry official said on Tuesday.
The official told Reuters the five-judge court would meet in London on January 14.

He said Yemen appointed an Egyptian and an American to the arbitration panel while Eritrea named an American and a Briton. Both countries have agreed on a fifth person to head the panel, but the official did not say what his nationality was.
Arab Yemen and African Eritrea had signed an accord in October in Paris to set up the arbitration court in London.
Both countries claim sovereignty over the small, arid Hanish islands. The dispute led to clashes in which at least 12 people died in December 1995.
